external_invariants: Model: GPT2LMHeadModel with n_layer=12, n_embd=768, n_head=12, vocab_size=50257, n_positions=1024, resid_pdrop=embd_pdrop=attn_pdrop=0.0, use_cache=False, attn_implementation='eager', FP32, train mode, initialized immediately after torch.manual_seed(20261020).

Data: per-rank synthetic token IDs drawn with torch.Generator().manual_seed(31000 + rank); accumulation_steps=4 tensors of shape (micro_batch=1, sequence_length=128) with values in [0, 50257); no other dataset exists (request assets are empty by design).

Numerics: FP32 end to end; torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32=False; torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32=False; torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark=False; torch.set_float32_matmul_precision('highest'); no autocast, no GradScaler, no compilation.

Accumulation: optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True) at step start; loss for each micro-batch is model(input_ids=tokens, labels=tokens, use_cache=False).loss / 4; first 3 micro-batches run under DDP no_sync, only the final micro-batch triggers gradient synchronization; reported loss is the sum of the 4 scaled micro losses and must be finite.

Optimizer: SGD(lr=0.001, momentum=0.0, weight_decay=0.0, foreach=False); exactly one optimizer.step() per workload repetition; SGD keeps no momentum state so the reset only reloads the initial weights.

DDP configuration: broadcast_buffers=False, bucket_cap_mb=25, gradient_as_bucket_view=True, device_ids=[bound device index]; find_unused_parameters stays False; no communication hooks are registered in the measured path (the source registers its inventory hook only in a separate diagnostic step).

Cross-rank semantics: after the final micro-batch every rank holds bitwise-identical gradients (source exact_gradient_replica_check with atol=0, rtol=0); effective global batch = world_size 2 x micro_batch 1 x accumulation_steps 4 = 8 micro-batches = 1024 tokens per step.
Reset fidelity: every repetition starts from the same initial weights (CPU state_dict snapshot), empty gradients, empty optimizer state and the prepare-time RNG states.

Timing hygiene: control coordination (barrier, peak-memory reset, synchronization) uses the separate gloo group and happens outside the timer; the only NCCL collectives in the measured workload are the DDP gradient allreduces of the final accumulation micro-batch; step_ms must stay <= 1.05x baseline.

Observations: loss, per-micro losses, every gradient tensor and every updated parameter of the ~124M-parameter model are exposed as full tensors; no elapsed times or performance counters appear in observations.
Quality scope: gradient/parameter comparisons use atol=1e-6, rtol=1e-4 (request.quality); reference fidelity only, no downstream accuracy or convergence claim.

Workload frozen: batch, sequence_length=128, accumulation_steps=4, world_size=2, architecture, FP32 precision, seeded data, completion boundary and quality checks are never altered to improve a score.

selection.rationale: Primary objective is clean step_ms (current accepted parent 147.20/146.56 ms, paired noise bounds 4.30/3.80 ms, communication goal gated at step_ms <= 1.05x baseline); the secondary goal diagnostic.max_rank_nccl_kernel_sum_ms is owned entirely by these two groups, which are the only NCCL kernels in the frozen workload: the 12 regular 28,351,488-byte DDP gradient-bucket allreduces of the final accumulation micro-step (group f833b57a373d8262a384, call d0938de87369efd500322679, collectives seq 21-32) plus the single 157,541,376-byte embedding-bucket allreduce (group 8525af72c631b94e3dd0, call b8ade439d7b8bd5fb5c1029b, seq 33) that together move all 497,759,232 gradient bytes per rank. Current discovery measures the max-rank diagnostic at 192.47 ms (rank 0: 12 kernels at 13.6-16.6 ms plus the 19.5 ms tail) versus 63.44 ms on rank 1 (12 kernels at the 3.5-3.6 ms wire floor, 19.5 ms tail symmetric, ~8 GB/s effective on both payload sizes), so roughly 129 ms of the objective is in-kernel peer wait, not wire bytes; the waiting rank flipped relative to the previous discovery (rank 1 then, first kernel 45.4 ms), proving the asymmetry is session-dependent arrival skew rather than a property of either group's payloads. The concrete previous failure lives on this boundary and was caused by the boundary split: a single-group selection let the candidate move 12 of the 13 collectives onto a freshly built second NCCL communicator while the embedding-bucket allreduce stayed on the default process group; that trial passed quality and lowered the discovery kernel sum (225.85 -> 139.87 ms) but regressed clean paired step_ms from 146.88 to 240.51 ms (paired gains -89.91/-97.35 ms), and all tuned parameter points landed at 247-252 ms, so the split-communicator mechanism itself - not the protocol/CTA knob values - was the regression; an attempted knob repair did not change the observed failure. The repair is therefore a joint, whole-path boundary: both groups execute as one ordered sequence on the workload's single default NCCL communicator stream, and any edit to one side measurably interacts with the other (the failed trial is the existence proof), so they must be one candidate. The joint boundary lets the next implementation keep all 13 bucket allreduces on the default communicator with parent-identical in-place SUM semantics per bucket (preserving the bitwise exact_gradient_replica_check at atol=0/rtol=0 and the frozen DDP configuration, bucket sizes and workload boundaries) and spend its degrees of freedom on absorbing rank-arrival skew before kernels launch instead of inside 12 stretched NCCL kernels. This selection is disjoint from the 21 compute groups owned by the installed quality-passing bundle trial-32cd1ce604-param-3a67a278, whose replacements must stay active; coexistence of a communication-path candidate with that bundle is already demonstrated (the rejected trial ran both bundles on both ranks with passing gradient/parameter checks), and per the composition protocol no positive step_ms gain is required to demonstrate compatibility, while no slower combination will be published.
selection.hypothesis: If all 13 gradient-bucket allreduces are kept on the workload's single default NCCL communicator and stream - no second communicator, no cross-communicator stalls, each call still a real async in-place SUM of the same bucket tensor returning the Work to the DDP reducer, with parent routing as the exact null point - and the rank-arrival skew that currently stretches the max-rank kernels (12 x ~14.2 ms vs the 3.6 ms wire floor, plus a 45-ms-scale first-kernel wait in the prior discovery) is absorbed by a cheap rank alignment at the start of the owned synchronization sequence rather than inside the NCCL kernels, then diagnostic.max_rank_nccl_kernel_sum_ms should fall from ~192.5 ms toward the ~63 ms per-rank wire floor (12 x ~3.6 ms + 19.5 ms tail) while clean step_ms stays within the 1.05x constraint: the late rank's timeline is untouched, the waiting rank's wait moves from GPU time inside kernels to bounded pre-issue alignment, and the 19.5 ms embedding-bucket tail remains the honest wire floor on both ranks. Testable and falsifiable: acceptance is only by the paired AB/BA clean step_ms protocol - a repeat of the previous -90/-97 ms paired regression fails immediately, and a diagnostic-only gain was already ruled insufficient when step_ms regressed; the communication objective must be re-collected in the separate clean collector runs because discovery-hook timings are not interchangeable with clean wall time. If clean collector samples show the skew is largely discovery-only, the diagnostic approaches the wire floor anyway (~63 ms) and step_ms is unchanged, which is an acceptable compatibility-neutral composition per protocol. All numbers above are treated as hypotheses to be tested, not predicted guarantees; the parent-routing null point reproduces baseline behavior exactly as the safety floor.

proposal.rationale: Repair of the concrete failure recorded in inputs/previous-feedback.txt, and how it changes this attempt: the rejected bundle trial-constraint-repair-0dbfc106-param-bb7dfba4 replaced only 12 of the 13 final-backward collectives and moved them onto a freshly initialized second NCCL communicator (direct ProcessGroupNCCL construction with NCCL_PROTO/NCCL_ALGO windows and ncclConfig CTA knobs) while the 157,541,376-byte embedding-bucket allreduce stayed on the default process group. It passed quality with max_abs_error 0.0 and even lowered the discovery kernel sum (225.85 -> 139.87 ms), but clean paired AB/BA step_ms regressed from 146.88 to 240.51 ms (paired gains -89.91/-97.35 ms, noise bounds 4.30/3.80 ms) and all tuned parameter points landed at 247-252 ms, so the split-communicator mechanism itself - not the transport knob values - was the regression; the supplemental resource_tradeoff note further warns that intrusive discovery timings are not clean critical-path evidence. This attempt therefore uses the joint two-group boundary exactly as selected: both call IDs (d0938de87369efd500322679, 12 x 28,351,488-byte regular buckets; b8ade439d7b8bd5fb5c1029b, the 157,541,376-byte embedding bucket) are replaced by one candidate that keeps every one of the 13 collectives on the workload's single default NCCL communicator and stream, issued through the same process-group backend object the parent c10d::allreduce_ operator resolves for this device, with parent-identical in-place ReduceOp.SUM semantics on the same bucket tensors and the same async Work contract returned to the DDP reducer. No second communicator is created, no env windows are touched, no streams or graphs are introduced, and no NCCL transport settings are modified (the default communicator was initialized by the worker before build(), so honest transport retuning is out of reach and is not claimed). The single degree of freedom left is where rank-arrival skew is absorbed: target-resources.json shows the max-rank diagnostic at 192.47 ms (rank 0: 12 kernels at 13.6-16.6 ms plus the 19.5 ms tail) versus 63.44 ms on rank 1 (12 kernels at the 3.5-3.6 ms wire floor, symmetric 19.5 ms tail), i.e. roughly 129 ms of the objective is peer-wait spun inside NCCL kernels, and the waiting rank flipped between discoveries, proving session-dependent arrival skew rather than a payload property. route=parent is the exact null point (bit-identical baseline routing, the safety floor for the paired revalidation); route=align_first inserts one CPU-side barrier on the adapter's gloo control group before the first collective of each 13-call synchronization sequence (marker-based detection: the embedding-bucket call is the last collective of every run, so the call immediately after it - or the first call ever - opens each sequence on both ranks symmetrically), moving the early rank's wait from GPU time inside the stretched kernels to bounded pre-issue CPU wait so both ranks' kernels run near their observed wire floor while the late rank's timeline is untouched; route=align_each applies the same barrier before every collective for tight per-bucket pairing. The barriers are gloo, not NCCL, so the measured workload's NCCL collective inventory is unchanged and no NCCL kernel is added or removed - all 13 allreduces still execute as real collectives on every invocation. Composition: this candidate's groups are disjoint from the 21 compute groups owned by the installed quality-passing bundle trial-32cd1ce604-param-3a67a278, which stays active and untouched (requires=[], replaces=[]); both bundles execute on both ranks, and coexistence of a communication-path candidate with that compute bundle is already demonstrated by the rejected trial's passing gradient/parameter checks over the same composition. Per the composition protocol no positive gain is required to demonstrate compatibility and no slower combination will be published. All effect magnitudes above are hypotheses to be tested, not predicted guarantees: acceptance is only via the paired clean AB/BA step_ms protocol with the 1.05x step_ms gate, and the communication objective is re-collected in separate clean collector runs; if the clean-run skew proves mostly discovery-only, the align routes are compatibility-neutral and the parent route reproduces the baseline exactly.

steps: build() reads context['state'] (device, gloo control group), context['targets'] for both call IDs, context['references'] for parent fallbacks, context['parameters'] for the route (default 'parent'), and binds record_route via context.get('record_route', lambda *_: None).

Two closures are created, one per call ID, sharing only two Python marker flags (started, last_was_embed) for sequence-position detection. No communicator is created, destroyed or split; no environment variable is read or written; no CUDA kernel, stream, graph, event or allocation is produced during build.

At call time each replacement validates the observed signature (single 1-D contiguous CUDA fp32 tensor of the call's expected numel, sparse_indices None); matching calls are issued on the default process group's device backend with AllreduceOptions(reduceOp=SUM, asyncOp=async_op), returning (tensors, work.boxed()) exactly like the parent operator; non-matching signatures fall back to the captured parent reference and are labeled 'parent-signature-fallback'.

In align modes, a dist.barrier(group=state['control']) runs on the CPU before the first collective of each synchronization sequence (align_first) or before every collective (align_each); it adds no NCCL kernel and no device work.

Both ranks run identical build() code with identical parameters and identical observed call sequences (12 + 1 per run per rank_specs), so routing and barrier positions are symmetric; the mapping is returned on both ranks.
setup_work.memory: Setup allocates only trivial Python objects (two closures and two boolean flags): no device tensors, no CUDA Graphs, no retained pools, and - unlike the rejected trial - no second NCCL communicator, so no additional NCCL driver allocations are introduced (framework.peak_allocated_bytes / peak_reserved_bytes and the lifecycle peaks are expected unchanged from the installed-bundle baseline). The declared warm-model metric is step_ms, not a memory counter, and no memory saving is claimed.
setup_work.timing_scope: All setup work runs inside build(), before validation and measurement. The measured run() still executes the frozen workload: optimizer.zero_grad, four forward/backward micro-batches (first three under DDP no_sync), the 13 gradient-bucket allreduces of the final micro-step's backward on the single default NCCL communicator, one optimizer.step(), and the closing synchronize. The only added work inside the timer is the CPU-side gloo barrier of the align routes on the owned synchronization path; the framework's own control coordination stays outside the timer and is not modified.

quality_risks: The boxed ReduceOp argument of c10d::allreduce_ is not introspectable from Python, so the replacement reconstructs AllreduceOptions with ReduceOp.SUM. This matches the frozen semantics (DDP default allreduce hook, no communication hooks in the measured path, ReduceOp.SUM recorded for every observation); a hypothetical non-SUM call would execute incorrectly and fail the source's atol=0 cross-rank check and the 1e-6/1e-4 reference checks loudly rather than silently.

Barrier symmetry: alignment positions are derived from a marker (the call following the embedding-bucket call, or the first call ever), and both ranks observe identical per-run sequences (12 regular + 1 embedding on each rank), so barriers always pair. If sequences ever diverged, the control group's bounded 120 s barrier timeout would raise and fail the run loudly; the framework restores the parent on failure. No silent numeric corruption path exists.

The align routes block the DDP reducer's calling thread until the peer reaches the same collective, which trades in-kernel GPU spin-wait for pre-issue CPU wait and could perturb communication/compute overlap. This is bounded by the workload's step_ms <= 1.05x baseline gate, measured by the paired AB/BA protocol; a repeat of the previous -90/-97 ms regression fails immediately, and route=parent is the exact null point reproducing baseline routing.

The align routes add a gloo collective inside the timed region (outside NCCL): the measured workload's NCCL collective inventory is unchanged, outputs, gradients, parameter updates and bitwise two-rank fp32 SUM on the same default communicator are preserved, but step_ms includes the barrier cost honestly; no diagnostic-counter decrease is claimed as a physical memory or wire-byte saving.

Quality/coverage: every one of the 13 collectives per run still executes as a real allreduce through the replacement (candidate call counting sees both call IDs; reference invocations occur only for non-observed signature fallbacks, which none of the observed calls use); no calls are eliminated, so no consumer-validity question arises.

Environment assumptions are minimal and guarded: torch._C._distributed_c10d ProcessGroup.unbox/_get_backend are used exactly as in the previously quality-passing implementation on this torch build; a missing control group or uninitialized distributed state silently disables alignment (route degrades to the parent-identical path) rather than crashing a run.

params.name: route
params.description: parent: issue every one of the 13 bucket allreduces on the workload's default NCCL communicator through the parent's process-group backend with identical in-place SUM options (bit-identical baseline routing, exact null point). align_first: additionally run one CPU-side gloo barrier on the adapter's control group before the first collective of each per-run synchronization sequence (first call ever, or the call right after the embedding-bucket allreduce), absorbing rank-arrival skew before kernels launch instead of inside NCCL kernels. align_each: run the same barrier before every one of the 13 collectives for tight per-bucket pairing. All routes keep every collective real, on the same communicator, with the same tensors and semantics.
